title: Move all background drains to headless claude -p invoked by the daemon; defer inline classifier judging
summary: Empirical finding plus direction. The v1 edge classifier is NOT safe to enforce inline: shadow vs LLM judge agreement is 65.3 percent (280 of 429 rows), barely above the 56.6 percent majority base rate; there is no confident band (abs of P keep minus the 0.65 threshold at least 0.1 covers only 1.4 percent of rows, at least 0.2 covers zero — the sigmoid outputs are crushed into the 0.5 to 0.8 range); enforcing it would wrongly prune 104 of 243 edges the LLM kept (43 percent); the learned cosine weight is negative (minus 0.52), a sign of overfit on a thin one day corpus (429 rows, all from 2026-06-15) with only 6 scalar features that omit the neighborhood and text signal the LLM judge actually uses. So inline deterministic classifier judging is DEFERRED until the corpus grows and structural features are added. DECISION: move all three standing drains (judge followup/harness-judge-drain, label followup/harness-label-drain, learner followup/harness-learner-drain) off interactive session and loop dispatch onto daemon invoked headless claude dash p processes, so background maintenance survives a closed session — this fixes the zero active loop never restarted failure. Real ready task impl work STAYS on session bound agent dispatch (high stakes, open ended). Rationale: the passive daemon cannot start an interactive agent but it CAN spawn a child process — onboard-learn.js already shells claude dash p, and the learner drain is already headless, so the pattern generalizes. Loop unreliability was also starving the shadow corpus (no judge running means no new shadow rows since 2026-06-15), a feedback loop the headless drains break. Safety: opt in flag default off, per drain token budget plus concurrency cap; nothing auto spends or auto merges.
